what_this_is: Roadmap 3.4, the stage review. One entry per review action: the human row it became, every verdict whose evidence names that row, and what the rule that wrote each verdict declares about itself. A human row that reached nothing is listed under `reached_nothing` — that is a finding about the pipeline, not a gap in this file. A disagreement NEVER changes a verdict.

absent.aug_dot: read off the cell raster; not derivable from rows
absent.beam_stroke: read off the cell raster by line_detection; not derivable
absent.flag: read off the cell raster; not derivable from rows
absent.glyph_band_distance: produced by gather_ownership_evidence from the cell RASTER (a same-class overlap search); not derivable from rows, so a human box never enters glyph_owner's contest
absent.glyph_conf: a person produced no softmax; writing a number here would convert 'there is no such measurement' into a definite one
absent.glyph_ladder: produced by gather_ownership_evidence from the cell RASTER (a ledger-rung search); not derivable from rows

table.label: a symbol of class …
table.reaches: adjudicate_notehead_is_not_a_notehead (refuses the head where the class is OUTSIDE the notehead family); the new class is filed as a HUMAN BOX of its own, which every decision whose domain that class enters then decides on

table.label: belongs to another staff
table.reaches: adjudicate_glyph_owner, reason `human_owner` — but ONLY on a glyph already in that decision's domain (`subjects_from=Q.GLYPH_BAND_DISTANCE`, the CONTESTED population). On an uncontested glyph the row is filed and reaches nothing, and the feedback file says so.

table.label: another staff — I can't say which
table.reaches: every per-family refusal AND adjudicate_notehead_is_not_a_notehead, reason `human_other_staff` — the glyph is refused on THIS staff and awarded to none. It does NOT reach adjudicate_glyph_owner, which must return a staff key.

table.label: a duplicate of another box
table.reaches: adjudicate_notehead_is_not_a_notehead, reason `human_not_a_symbol`, `detail.human_says` naming the twin — one piece of ink, one note

table.label: I can't tell
table.reaches: NOTHING, deliberately. An Abstention with reason `human_unsure`: a place the PRINT is ambiguous, reported by review/feedback.py and read by no stage.

table.label: yes, that is what it is
table.reaches: NOTHING, by design. It is a READ row where there would otherwise be no row at all, so `review/feedback.py` can say which boxes a human went over and agreed with — the denominator every other label is a numerator of.
table.keys: Enter on the class already shown

labels.\u26a0\ufe0f: `unsure_box` files an ABSTENTION, so it appears in no `wants` list and reaches nothing by design — ABSTAIN.HUMAN_UNSURE says why.

conventions.title: A clef's SIZE is consistent with its staff, and it stands at the system's first-measure edge
conventions.says: Sean, 2026-09-23 (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, ROADMAP 2.11): *"it also looks like the clef box is too small. the size of clefs are consistent to the staff and the edge of the first measure on the system — that should be helpful geometrically."* A clef is scaled to the staff it stands on, not to the ink around it, and it is printed at the head of that staff's first measure.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose C clef measures outside 3.3–4.7 staff spaces (it would show as a clef this band then refuses to defend), or a header cluster inside the band at the system's clef x that a human confirms is NOT a clef.

conventions.title: A beam joins stem TIPS, so every stem on one stroke points the same way
conventions.says: a beam is drawn across the ends of the stems it joins, so a beamed group is stem-unanimous.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a beamed group whose stems genuinely disagree — which would mean the beam is not joining tips.

conventions.title: A whole rest HANGS under the 4th line; a half rest SITS on the 3rd — and they are the same shape
conventions.says: both are a filled rectangle half a staff space tall, and they differ **ONLY** in which line they touch.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate printing whole rests at a different slot; or any shape measurement that separates whole from half.

conventions.title: A multi-bar rest is an H-bar one staff space thick
conventions.says: several bars of silence are shown as a thick horizontal bar between two vertical strokes, with a number above.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose multi-bar rests are drawn at beam thickness.

conventions.title: A key signature's accidentals stand at fixed slots, in a fixed order, keyed on the CLEF
conventions.says: the sharps and flats of a key signature are printed in one invariable sequence, at positions fixed by convention for each clef.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.title: Timpani, horns and trumpets are conventionally written WITHOUT a key signature
conventions.says: in this repertoire the natural-horn, natural-trumpet, timpani and tuned-percussion staves carry no key signature at all — the accidentals are written in.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.

conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.

checked_by: "the accidental ORDER is fixed (F#-C#-G#... / Bb-Eb-Ab...): a run that SKIPS a slot is impossible [C21]"
"a key signature's accidentals stand at fixed SLOTS, so two boxes at one x are ONE slot [C21]"
"across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- transposing parts print different signatures for one key"
"a key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it [C24] -- so a concert key with no peer on its own system is a misreading"
"the clef and key signature are reprinted at the head of EVERY system [C25 + L38] -- so a staff disagreeing with its own document's majority is a misreading of that staff"

conventions.title: A key signature's accidentals stand at fixed slots, in a fixed order, keyed on the CLEF
conventions.says: the sharps and flats of a key signature are printed in one invariable sequence, at positions fixed by convention for each clef.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.title: Timpani, horns and trumpets are conventionally written WITHOUT a key signature
conventions.says: in this repertoire the natural-horn, natural-trumpet, timpani and tuned-percussion staves carry no key signature at all — the accidentals are written in.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.

checked_by: "the accidental ORDER is fixed (F#-C#-G#... / Bb-Eb-Ab...): a run that SKIPS a slot is impossible [C21]"

"across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- transposing parts print different signatures for one key"

"the clef and key signature are reprinted at the head of EVERY system [C25 + L38] -- so a staff disagreeing with its own document's majority is a misreading of that staff"

conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.

checked_by: "the accidental ORDER is fixed (F#-C#-G#... / Bb-Eb-Ab...): a run that SKIPS a slot is impossible [C21]"
"a key signature's accidentals stand at fixed SLOTS, so two boxes at one x are ONE slot [C21]"
"across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- transposing parts print different signatures for one key"
"a key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it [C24] -- so a concert key with no peer on its own system is a misreading"
"the clef and key signature are reprinted at the head of EVERY system [C25 + L38] -- so a staff disagreeing with its own document's majority is a misreading of that staff"

conventions.title: A key signature's accidentals stand at fixed slots, in a fixed order, keyed on the CLEF
conventions.says: the sharps and flats of a key signature are printed in one invariable sequence, at positions fixed by convention for each clef.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.title: Timpani, horns and trumpets are conventionally written WITHOUT a key signature
conventions.says: in this repertoire the natural-horn, natural-trumpet, timpani and tuned-percussion staves carry no key signature at all — the accidentals are written in.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.

checked_by: "the accidental ORDER is fixed (F#-C#-G#... / Bb-Eb-Ab...): a run that SKIPS a slot is impossible [C21]"

"across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- transposing parts print different signatures for one key"

"the clef and key signature are reprinted at the head of EVERY system [C25 + L38] -- so a staff disagreeing with its own document's majority is a misreading of that staff"

conventions.title: A ledger line is only ever OUTSIDE the staff
conventions.says: Sean, 2026-09-24 (`docs/DECISIONS.md`), on 13 ledger-line crops: *"the ledger lines will only be on the outside of the staff"*. A `ledgerLine` box whose centre lies in the band between line 1 and line 5 is not a ledger line, whatever its distance to a staff line.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a printed ledger line inside the band — which no engraving convention produces; more plausibly, a `Q.STAFF_LINES` registration wrong by a whole space, which would put real rungs inside the modelled band.

conventions.title: A ledger line exists only where there is a NOTE on it
conventions.says: Sean, 2026-09-24 (`docs/DECISIONS.md`): *"… and only happen if there are actual notes in the staff"* — a bar holding only a whole rest has no ledger lines, and a rung with no notehead on or near it is not a rung.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a printed rung with no note on or beyond it; operationally, Sean calling a `no_head_on_the_rung` crop a real ledger line whose head is visibly printed.

"a meter is a SYSTEM fact: a mid-staff change no other staff witnessed is a misread (21 fired on scans, 0 survive)"

conventions.title: A beam joins stem TIPS, so every stem on one stroke points the same way
conventions.says: a beam is drawn across the ends of the stems it joins, so a beamed group is stem-unanimous.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a beamed group whose stems genuinely disagree — which would mean the beam is not joining tips.

conventions.title: A whole rest HANGS under the 4th line; a half rest SITS on the 3rd — and they are the same shape
conventions.says: both are a filled rectangle half a staff space tall, and they differ **ONLY** in which line they touch.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate printing whole rests at a different slot; or any shape measurement that separates whole from half.

conventions.title: A multi-bar rest is an H-bar one staff space thick
conventions.says: several bars of silence are shown as a thick horizontal bar between two vertical strokes, with a number above.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose multi-bar rests are drawn at beam thickness.

conventions.title: A clef's SIZE is consistent with its staff, and it stands at the system's first-measure edge
conventions.says: Sean, 2026-09-23 (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, ROADMAP 2.11): *"it also looks like the clef box is too small. the size of clefs are consistent to the staff and the edge of the first measure on the system — that should be helpful geometrically."* A clef is scaled to the staff it stands on, not to the ink around it, and it is printed at the head of that staff's first measure.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose C clef measures outside 3.3–4.7 staff spaces (it would show as a clef this band then refuses to defend), or a header cluster inside the band at the system's clef x that a human confirms is NOT a clef.

checked_by: "the clef and key signature are reprinted at the head of EVERY system [C25 + L38], so one fact has many independent readings"
"a key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it [C24] -- so a change on a few staves alone is a misreading of those staves"
"across the staves of a system the DELTA is shared, never the value -- so a change is corroborated on the SHIFT and needs no transposition"
"timpani, horns and trumpets are conventionally written WITHOUT a key signature [C81], so they neither vote nor are judged by the concert tally"

conventions.title: A key signature's accidentals stand at fixed slots, in a fixed order, keyed on the CLEF
conventions.says: the sharps and flats of a key signature are printed in one invariable sequence, at positions fixed by convention for each clef.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a plate whose signature accidentals do not sit on the conventional slots for the read clef, or print them in another order.

conventions.title: A key CHANGE is printed at ONE bar of ONE system, on EVERY staff of it
conventions.says: the engraver announces a key change simultaneously across the whole system, at one bar.
conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a real mid-staff key change that fails its own witness test.

conventions.title: Timpani, horns and trumpets are conventionally written WITHOUT a key signature

conventions.would_be_falsified_by: a held 19th-century edition printing key signatures on its horn and timpani staves.
